Watcom field-by-field struct copy (3 consecutive `dst.field = src.field;` lines). Replace with `dst = src;` or `memcpy(&dst, &src, sizeof(...));` in a .keep — but only once the run (together with any sibling runs for the same dst/src pair) covers every byte of the struct. Collapsing a run that leaves a gap WIDENS the copy and changes behaviour; see `partial_struct_copy` (§31) for that case.
Watcom cascade constant fill (3 sibling fields chained through prior store of `0.0`). Replace with 3 direct stores of the constant in a .keep.
(int)&NAME used in arithmetic — Watcom byte-offset trampolining that should be expressed as struct field or array index access. Replace in a .keep.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pSVar6` self-updates via the address of a sibling field whose byte offset equals the array stride. Replace `pSVar6->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar3` self-updates via element-arithmetic `(int)(pCVar3 + N) + M`, where `N*sizeof(*pCVar3) + M` equals the larger struct stride being walked (the pointer is typed to a sub-element). Replace `pCVar3->field` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.
